Close Harry Wood's Diary The Albert Pub & Geomob + Blue Posts tonight Posted by Harry Wood on 23 September 2026 in English . Last updated on 11 November 2026. Tonight’s London pub meet-up is at the Blue Posts . An old favourite! Last time I said I was going to be adventurous with pub choices, and we went to The Albert in Victoria. I’m sorry I didn’t bother writing down any notes about interesting OpenStreetMap discussions from the evening. Rest assured many interesting OpenStreetMap discussions were discussed. My diary entry last time was just about pub choices, and this one will be no different! Actually I do remember there was a lot of conversation about delivering election leaflets, since we had at least three different people in attendance who do a lot of campaigning, and using OpenStreetMap for that. It’s quite a nice use of OSM since you can boost the addressing coverage in the area of interest, and then use it, and then fix issues while using it, in a nice localised virtuous circle, and the use involves visiting every address, so perfect for filling in any map gaps. So this was a new pub, and it worked pretty well. I decided to follow a theory I had, that pubs can be less overcrowded and more pleasant when they are further away from tube stations . pages.text: Has James Trafford replaced Jordan Pickford as England No 1? - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, James Trafford has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026 By Joe Rindl BBC Sport journalist Published 16 November 2026 It was some night for James Trafford. As he was mobbed by his England team-mates for a late double save that secured a memorable 3-2 win against world champions Spain, the debate that followed about who the country's number one is was inevitable. The Leeds keeper was given his chance to show England boss Thomas Tuchel what he could do again - and he absolutely took it. On his fifth England cap the 24-year-old enjoyed a magnificent performance in Madrid as his side handed the hosts their first loss in 43 matches. Trafford made four key saves in the final 12 minutes of the game, including an incredible double stop to first deny a Lamine Yamal curler and then dive again to his right to keep out Fermin Lopez from close range. Last week Tuchel had made it clear that Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford was his number one. But after full-time in Spain Tuchel told ITV Sport "there's no number one" and Trafford had "a brilliant match". pages.text: Here's how dinosaur ‘mummies’ are helping scientists solve fossil mysteries | National Geographic SCIENCE How did these dinosaurs become ‘mummies’? Two new fossils help solve the mystery A new study sheds light on how these reptiles become “mummies” and paints a picture of what these ancient animals looked like. Paul Sereno and his colleagues spent years painstakingly preparing this Edmontosaurus annectens "mummy" unearthed in Wyoming, dubbed "Ed Junior" because it's a juvenile. The researchers also found an adult mummy from the same species, which they nicknamed "Ed Senior." Rebecca Hale, National Geographic By Riley Black Published October 23, 2025 The bulk of what we know from dinosaurs comes from bones. Skeletal parts can reveal a dinosaur’s size, how fast they grew, and even if they were gravid with eggs when they perished, but all the ribs, jaws, and other pieces can only go so far in revealing what our favorite dinosaurs looked like in life. Fortunately, paleontologists have found some dinosaur bones are preserved with soft tissues like feathers, claw sheaths, and, with luck, entire dinosaur “mummies.” These aren’t traditional mummies purposefully preserved through chemical embalming. Instead, they’re fossils that preserve skin impressions as a thin layer within the rock. As paleontologists have continued to sift through the fossil record, such specimens are finally offering some insights into the external appearance of familiar species. pages.text: Here’s Lookin’ at You, Dollocaris | National Geographic How Dollocaris captured prey. From Vannier et al., 2015. SCIENCE LAELAPS Here’s Lookin’ at You, Dollocaris By Riley Black Published February 29, 2016 • 4 min read I’ve never been particularly interested in space. I think the fossil record is to blame. Not because paleontology takes up all the compartments in my brain for wonder or anything like that. It’s more that I don’t really care all that much about distant planets that may or may not harbor life when we have a fantastic record of strange creatures right here on Earth. Just look at Dollocaris . I hadn’t even heard of the little Jurassic invertebrate until a few months ago, when paleontologist Jean Vannier and colleagues published a new analysis on the critter, but it immediately made me think of a little spacecraft. The small body, big eyes, and grappling appendages make the small arthropod look like one of the little repair ships you might see mending the surface of larger starcraft in the background of a big-budget scifi epic. But this was nothing alien or that we had to conjure through CGI. Dollocaris was real, and lived on our planet around 160 million years ago. Exactly what Dollocaris was, no one really knows. The most specific paleontologists can get is somewhere in the realm of arthropods. But from there the spineless fossil has been associated with everything from mantis shrimp to remipedes – blind, worm-like crustaceans that live in the darkness of aquatic caves. Library of Congress, Wright Collection Modern aviation took off with the first controlled, powered & sustained flight on December 17 th , 1903 in Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. Little did the Wright brothers know, when their dreams of heavier-than-air flight came to fruition over the beaches of North Carolina, they would become the beginning of a robust aviation history. Since then, aviation has gone from a twelve second flight in a wooden and cloth, open-air flying machine to aircraft fabricated from composite materials designed to safely ferry humans from earth to space and back. pages.text: History of OLMS | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content History of OLMS More in This Section Close Celebrating the LMRDA’s 60th Anniversary OLMS' history dates back to the September 14, 1959 passage of the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act of 1959, as amended (LMRDA), which was enacted by Congress to ensure certain basic standards of democracy and fiscal responsibility in labor organizations representing employees in private industry. The organization's original name was the Bureau of Labor-Management Reports (BLMR). It was re-named the Labor-Management Services Administration (LMSA) in 1963. At one time or another LMSA had responsibilities which included pension and welfare plans, Federal labor relations, veterans reemployment rights, and an anti-racketeering/organized crime strike force. Through reorganizations and the creation of new agencies through legislation, these functions were subsequently transferred to other Federal agencies. With the passage of the Civil Service Reform Act (CSRA) in 1978, the federal labor relations program was transferred to the newly created Federal Labor Relations Authority. However, the Standard of Conduct provisions of the CSRA which regulate internal affairs of federal-sector unions remained in LMSA. In 1980, the Foreign Service Act (FSA) was passed and unions representing employees of the Department of State and U.S. Information Agency (USIA) became subject to Standards of Conduct requirements. pages.text: Home 2021 - التنمية المستدامة Skip to content Home 2021 Mostafa Mohamed 2024-01-24T10:33:32-05:00 17 هدفا لتحويل العالم أهداف التنمية المستدامة هي دعوة عالمية للعمل للقضاء على الفقر وصون الأرض وتحسين المعايش في كل مكان. وقد تبنت كافة الدول الأعضاء في الأمم المتحدة هذه الأهداف السبعة عشر في عام 2015، بوصفها جزء من جدول أعمال التنمية المستدامة لعام 2030 ، الذي حدد خُطَّة مدتها 15 عامًا لتحقيق تلك الأهداف. حماية التنوع البيولوجي الهش تتصدر المشهد في محادثات أرمينيا تقرير أممي جديد يدعو إلى اقتصاد شامل يضمن استفادة الجميع من التحولات الاقتصادية والرقمية اليوم العالمي للموئل - دعوة من مسقط للتحرك بشأن أزمة الإسكان العالمية غوتيريش: النهوض بالتنمية وحقوق الإنسان والسلام معا رؤية يمكن أن توحدنا في عالم منقسم "لحظة أهداف التنمية المستدامة"، دعوة للوفاء بوعد التنمية في مواجهة رياح معاكسة قوية الحق في التنمية: لماذا يُعدّ الإنصاف، لا الإحسان، حقا من حقوق الإنسان؟ هدف الشهر—الحياة في البر تؤدي النظم الإيكولوجية للأرض دورًا حيويًا في استدامة حياة البشر. وفي تشرين الأول/أكتوبر، يُعقد مؤتمر الأمم المتحدة للتنوع البيولوجي (COP17) البلدان في يريفان، أرمينيا، لإجراء أول استعراض عالمي للتقدم المحرز نحو تحقيق الهدف 15. تجدون تفصيلا أوفي في افتتاحية «هدف الشهر» . إجراءات عملية عقدمن العمل يدعو عقد العمل إلى تسريع تحقيق أهداف التنمية المستدامة من خلال إيجاد حلول مستدامة لجميع التحديات الكبرى في العالم انطلاقا من الفقر والجنسانية و وصولا إلى تغير المناخ وعدم المساواة وسد الفجوة المالية حملة اعملوا الآن الحملة هي نداء أممي للعمل الفردي لتغير المناخ، وهي جزء أساسي من الجهود التي تنسقها الأمم المتحدة لإذكاء الوعي فيما يتصل بتغير المناخ والإسراع بتنفيذ اتفاق باريس نادي الكتاب لأهداف التنمية المستدام

pages.text: Homeless Veterans' Reintegration Program | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Homeless Veterans' Reintegration Program More in This Section Close Homeless Veterans' Reintegration Program Application Recipient Information About HVRP The U.S. Department of Labor, Veterans’ Employment and Training Service (VETS), Homeless Veterans’ Reintegration Program (HVRP) is the only federal grant to focus exclusively on competitive employment for veterans experiencing homelessness. The HVRP has strong partnerships between public, private, and nonprofit organizations, especially those that employ and partner with veterans who have experienced homelessness, to deliver services to veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness assisting them in overcoming barriers to employment. Participants of the program receive services such as career exploration, career technical training, job placement, and supportive services, with the goal of empowering them to secure employment in high-demand occupations, paying wages consistent with the relevant market. HVRP was initially authorized in 1987 under Section 738 of Stewart B. McKinney Homeless Assistance Act, and now is authorized under Title 38 U.S.C. Sections 2021, 2021A, and 2023. pages.text: How an Unlikely Fossil Hunter Found a Tyrannosaurus Trail | National Geographic SCIENCE How an Unlikely Fossil Hunter Found a Tyrannosaurus Trail A curious rock in the North Dakota badlands turned out to be a first-of-its-kind find. Three of five footprints in the first-ever adult Tyrannosaurus rex trackway are illuminated under the starry sky of North Dakota. The region is known for producing Triceratops and T. rex bones, but footprints of any kind are rare. The bill is then put before that chamber to be voted on. If the bill passes one body of Congress, it goes to the other body to go through a similar process of research, discussion, changes, and voting. Once both bodies vote to accept a bill, they must work out any differences between the two versions. Then both chambers vote on the same version of the bill. If it passes, they present it to the president. The president then considers the bill. The president can approve the bill and sign it into law. Or the president can refuse to approve a bill. pages.text: Huge waves pummel California coast, forcing closure of popular piers | California | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Waves crash on to the Pacifica Pier in Pacifica, California, on Saturday. Photograph: Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle/AP View image in fullscreen Waves crash on to the Pacifica Pier in Pacifica, California, on Saturday. Photograph: Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle/AP California Huge waves pummel California coast, forcing closure of popular piers Large waves up to 50ft flooded southern California streets and prompted evacuation warning near coastal city Associated Press Sun 15 Nov 2026 20.00 EST Last modified on Mon 16 Nov 2026 16.39 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The California coast was pummeled again on Sunday by huge waves that inundated beaches, flooded local streets and forced the closure of popular piers. The National Weather Service office for the San Francisco Bay Area warned that surf up to 35ft (11 meters) was possible, along with dangerous rip currents and sneaker waves. “Stay out of the water, stay off rocks and jetties, and never turn your back on the ocean!” the weather service said on social media . On Saturday, waves above 50ft were recorded in San Mateo county , just south of San Francisco. Surfers weren’t deterred, taking advantage of giant waves at the famous Mavericks beach near Half Moon Bay. Farther south, the Santa Cruz county sheriff’s office issued an evacuation warning near the coastal town of Capitola that took the brunt of the powerful surf . pages.description: John Holmes and his wife explain why they have returned to Ukraine after initially fleeing.
pages.text: Hull man and wife who fled Ukraine return to a warzone Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live 'Friends think we're idiots for returning to Ukraine' 21 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Kevin Shoesmith East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire John Holmes Liliya Holmes and her British husband John pictured in Odesa, Ukraine When Russian forces launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, John Holmes – a British national – and his Ukrainian wife Liliya fled the port city of Odesa, fearing for their lives. But after four years in the UK, the draw of home has proven too strong and they have returned to Ukraine's third largest city, undeterred by the sustained threat of air raids. "Friends of ours thought we were idiots for going back to Ukraine," reflects John, 74. "But returning is something we felt we needed to do. "Yes, it's dangerous. Yes, there are drones flying overhead. Yes, you can hear the explosions. But you just have to get on with life as best you can. "Home is Ukraine." During their time away, the pair sought sanctuary in Hull , East Yorkshire, where John was born and raised and has a property. He met Liliya, 64, in Ukraine and had been living there for 30 years until the invasion. "We had built a good life here," he says. The database is designed to support HFP's safety surveillance program. Adverse events are coded to terms in the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) terminology . HFCS Data Files Frequently Asked Questions Please Note: Cosmetic product adverse event data will no longer be available in the HFCS. HFCS Data Files FDA provides raw data extracted from the HFCS database to the extent permitted by law and FDA regulations. The data files, which are available in Excel format, may include: demographic and administrative information and the HFCS report ID number; product information from the case reports; symptom information from the reports; patient outcome information from the reports. The data files contain data reported by consumers and health care practitioners, data voluntarily reported by industry, and data from mandatory reports from dietary supplement industry from January 2004 forward. It’s a colloquial term in the outdoor community. You see it everywhere, from campground signage to park brochures, and wilderness permits to ranger programs. It’s intermingled with phrases like “pack it in, pack it out” and “take only photos.” Leave No Trace has become so common in the outdoor community, that many forget that not everyone knows what it means. If you’ve found yourself staring blankly at a ranger saying, “Remember to Leave No Trace” as they send you on your way—this article is for you. Did You Know? Leave No Trace is a set of principles that empower people visiting the outdoors to leave nature as unchanged by our presence as possible. It’s a way of protecting the natural world to keep our outdoor spaces enjoyable for generations to come. While the phrase almost speaks for itself, there is a lot more to learn about what it really means to practice Leave No Trace.
